findings.summary: the run records one negative control (the reused request_id) where the plan's Done-when asks each change that reproduced at the base to have its own; the batch and enumerated-field controls named in the plan are not demonstrated in the record.
findings.text: The plan §7 Done-when requires each change that reproduced at the base to carry its own negative control ("Reporting only the first refused op fails the batch case"; "Dropping the legal values from an enumerated-field refusal fails that case"), but only the reused-id mutation is logged (logs/negative_control.log, EXIT=1). The batch and enumerated-field guards are independently falsifiable by reading (removing the refused_ops attach raises KeyError; removing _enumerated_field_legal_values drops "0.25" from the refusal), so durability is intact, but the per-change negative-control evidence the measure names is only partially recorded.

findings.summary: _value_at_path mirrors a subset of the address forms _apply_set accepts (the section/followup/gate/question/research list heads and the decisions/section_declarations maps) without an owner both can extend, so the two resolutions must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.text: reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:935 enumerates the set-path address forms independently of reckon/_store.py:2547 _apply_set's own dispatch, so a new form added to the write side is not seen by the read side that reports changed_targets. It correctly delegates the by-id lookup to the store's _find_by_id (reckon/_store.py:2396), so the prior review's specific concern is repaired; the remaining duplication is the form list only.
